turns.prompt: when I end a meeting, the recap leaves out any task that has a person on it but no deadline. like if they say 'Priya will send the contract' with no date it just isnt in the action items. can you fix it
turns.final_message:
I fixed it. The model was already listing those tasks. A filter that ran after the summary was generated deleted them.

**Cause:** in `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`, after the summary came back, a regex kept only action items that contained a date-like word (`by`, `due`, `tomorrow`, a weekday and so on) or any digit. "Priya will send the contract" has none of those, so it was dropped. The prompts in `electron/llm/prompts.ts` already tell the model to keep tasks that have an owner but no due date, so this filter was undoing that.

**Changes:**
- `electron/MeetingPersistence.ts:235`: replaced the deadline regex with a filter that only removes empty or non-text entries. Every real action item now gets through.
- The default summary prompt in the same file now asks for items in the form "Owner: task", with the due date if one was given. It says to keep items that have an owner but no date, matching the other prompts.

That filter only ran on the default recap path. Recaps made with a mode's own note sections never went through it, so they weren't affected.

I couldn't type-check or run it because `node_modules` isn't installed in this copy. The change is small, but the real test is to end a meeting where someone says "Priya will send the contract" and check that it shows up.

My first fix only covered half the problem. This time I traced the whole flow: the AI prompt, saving, the database and the screen that shows the recap. The other cause was in the prompt.

**What was wrong:** the app creates a default "General" mode and turns it on, so recaps nearly always use the mode prompt, not the default one I fixed last time. That mode prompt said nothing about tasks without dates. Its "Action items" section only says "Tasks and follow-ups identified." So the model treated "Priya will send the contract" as too vague and left it out. Saving, the database and the recap screen don't drop anything.

**What I changed:**
- **Mode prompt** (`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`): any section about tasks, follow-ups or next steps now has to include every task someone took on, even with no date. Items are written as "Priya: send the contract", and a date is added only if someone said one. I put the rule in the code that builds the prompt, not in the section text, because section text is saved in each user's database and editing it wouldn't change existing installs.
- **Groq prompt** (`electron/llm/prompts.ts`): this one is used on the default path when Groq is the model. Its only example had a deadline ("by Wednesday"), so I added the same rule.
- The deadline filter I removed last time stays removed.

**One thing still drops other people's tasks:** in the Sales and Team Meeting modes, the action items section says "All action items that were said **I** would do after the meeting", and Recruiting's says "that I have to do". In those modes the model is told to list only your own tasks, so Priya's would still be skipped, by design. If you use one of those, I can change the wording to cover everyone's tasks. That means a database migration so existing modes get the new text too.

I haven't type-checked or run this because `node_modules` isn't installed here. To test, rebuild, end a short meeting where someone says "Priya will send the contract", and look for "Priya: send the contract" in the recap. The log line `[MeetingPersistence] Active mode: ...` shows which mode and prompt were used.

I found four more things that were still dropping tasks and fixed them all. I've only tested the new parsing on its own in Node. The app itself hasn't been compiled or run, since there's no TypeScript compiler here and npm is blocked by the sandbox.

**What was still dropping tasks:**

1. **The end of the meeting was cut off.** The recap only got the first 10,000 characters of the transcript, about the first 10 to 15 minutes. Tasks usually get handed out in the wrap-up, like "ok so Priya will send the contract", which was exactly the part being cut. It now sends up to 40,000 characters and keeps the start plus the whole end (`electron/MeetingPersistence.ts`).
2. **Custom providers got the wrong instructions.** If you use a custom provider, the summary request also picked up the active mode's live-assistant instructions ("speak as the user", short spoken answers) and a second copy of the mode context. That pulled the model away from note-taking. The summary call now skips that (`electron/LLMHelper.ts`).
3. **Section names had to match exactly.** If the model labelled the section "Action Items" but your mode calls it "Action items", the whole section came back empty with no error. Matching now ignores case and punctuation.
4. **My own filter from last time dropped some tasks.** It threw away any task the model returned as an object, like `{"owner": "Priya", "task": "send the contract"}`, instead of plain text. Those are now converted to "Priya: send the contract", with "(due Friday)" added only if a date was given.

I also changed the step that shortens older transcript in very long meetings (over 1,800 transcript segments) so it keeps every task with its owner. Before, it could lose them before the recap even ran.

In the Node test, a task with no date, one with a date, one marked "no date given", and a mismatched section name all came through correctly. A task said at the very end of a long transcript was kept.

**Still open:** if you use the Sales, Team Meet or Recruiting mode, their Action Items section asks only for tasks *you* have to do, so Priya's task is still left out by design. Say if you want that changed to everyone's tasks.

If it still fails after rebuilding (`npm run app:dev`), send me the log lines that start with `[MeetingPersistence] Active mode:` and `Raw LLM summary response`. Those show whether the model never wrote the task or the app lost it afterward.
